alerts.name: Remote OS Command Injection
alerts.desc: Arbitrary operating system commands can be executed on the server by supplying shell metacharacters in parameter input.
alerts.solution: Avoid passing user input to system shell execution functions. Use native programming language APIs with strict parameter lists instead of shell command strings.

alerts.name: SQL Injection
alerts.desc: SQL injection may be possible. The user-supplied input in the search query parameter is directly concatenated into a dynamic SQL command without parameterized sanitization.

instances.evidence: Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax

alerts.solution: Refactor database access to use parameterized prepared statements or an Object-Relational Mapper (ORM) with strict query binding.

alerts.name: Cross Site Scripting (Reflected)
alerts.desc: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was identified in the artists parameter. Malicious JavaScript injected via parameter is echoed verbatim into the client DOM without HTML entity encoding.
alerts.solution: Contextually encode all user-controlled data before rendering into HTML. Implement a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP).

alerts.name: Directory Listing and Path Traversal
alerts.desc: Unrestricted access to file system directories permits unauthenticated attackers to read sensitive configuration and system files.
alerts.solution: Enforce canonical file path resolution, validate against a strict whitelist of permitted files, and disable web server directory listing.

alerts.name: Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens
alerts.desc: No Anti-CSRF tokens were found in HTML state-changing forms. Attackers can forge cross-origin POST requests on behalf of authenticated users.
alerts.solution: Implement cryptographically strong Synchronizer CSRF tokens or configure SameSite=Lax/Strict cookie attributes.

alerts.name: Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
alerts.desc: The HTTP response does not include the X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors header. The site can be framed by third parties to hijack clicks.
alerts.solution: Configure the web server to emit 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors none;'.

alerts.name: Cookie No HttpOnly Flag
alerts.desc: A cookie has been set without the HttpOnly attribute. This permits client-side JavaScript scripts to access the cookie value, increasing risk of credential exfiltration via XSS.
alerts.solution: Ensure that the HttpOnly flag is set on sensitive session and token cookies.

alerts.name: Server Banner and Version Disclosure
alerts.desc: The server response leaks detailed server banners and PHP runtime version numbers in HTTP response headers.
alerts.solution: Configure ServerTokens Prod and expose_php = Off in server configurations.
